haiku-low.q1: After the Message Store commit succeeds (step 4), via the gateway. The ack carries {msg_id, seq}, confirming the message is stored with that seq.
haiku-low.q2: The sender gets an error and nothing is published or fanned out. The retry must reuse the same msg_id; the store then returns the original seq without inserting a new row.
haiku-low.q3: After 30 seconds without a heartbeat, when its Presence Registry key expires. Heartbeats every 10 seconds reset the TTL; a clean disconnect deletes the key immediately.
haiku-low.q4: Nothing changes for the worker, which does not wait for the ack. The Offline Inbox entry stays, and after 5 seconds the gateway requests a push.
haiku-low.q5: The failure is logged and not retried. The Offline Inbox entry is left untouched, so the message remains pending for reconnect.
haiku-low.q6: Pending entries are read from the Offline Inbox, bodies fetched from Message Store, and sent per conversation in ascending seq. Clients drop duplicate msg_ids and place live messages by seq.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row is written in the same transaction as the message, so it survives a crash. The relay then publishes it later, so fan-out still happens.
haiku-low.q8: In the Presence Registry, an in-memory key-value store mapping user_id to gateway node with a 30 s TTL. Missing heartbeats let the key expire and remove the entry.
haiku-low.q9: The worker looks up the user in Presence and sends the message to gateway G's delivery queue, which writes it to the socket. Arrival is confirmed when the client acks msg_id within 5 seconds, deleting the Inbox entry.
haiku-low.q10: In the Offline Inbox, written for each recipient during fan-out before any delivery attempt. An entry is removed when the client acks that msg_id, or expires after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: It reads the user's pending Offline Inbox entries, then fetches the corresponding message bodies from Message Store by msg_id.
haiku-low.q12: The event is not acked, so the bus redelivers it and another worker repeats the whole recipient list. Inbox puts are idempotent on (user_id, msg_id), so duplicates are harmless.

sonnet.q1: After step 3's single transaction commits (message insert plus outbox row), the sender gets ack {msg_id, seq}. It tells them the message is durably stored with that seq; it does not mean anyone received it (fan-out is async).
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error; nothing is published (no outbox row, so no fan-out), so no one receives it. The retry must carry the same client-generated msg_id; the store returns the original seq instead of inserting again.
sonnet.q3: After 30 s without a heartbeat (heartbeats every 10 s reset the 30 s TTL), the presence key expires and the user counts as offline.
sonnet.q4: A push is requested and the Offline Inbox entry stays (it is deleted only on client ack).
sonnet.q5: It is logged and not retried; the Inbox entry is untouched.
sonnet.q6: In ascending seq per conversation (R4). Duplicates are dropped by the client by msg_id (live messages during R2-R4 are placed by seq and deduped by msg_id).
sonnet.q7: The outbox row was committed in the same transaction as the message, so the Outbox Relay still publishes it and fan-out happens; the client's retry gets the original ack.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry, an in-memory key-value store (user_id -> gateway node). With no heartbeat for 30 s the TTL expires and the key is removed (a clean disconnect deletes it explicitly).
sonnet.q9: The Fan-out Worker looks up the user in the Presence Registry, finds node G, and sends the message to G's delivery queue; G writes it to the socket and starts a 5 s timer. The client's ack of the msg_id within 5 s confirms arrival (and deletes the Inbox entry).
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox, as per-user pending entries (pointers: user_id, conv_id, seq, msg_id), written by the Fan-out Worker for every recipient before any delivery attempt. An entry is removed only when the client acks that msg_id (live or after reconnect); entries also expire after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: It reads the user's pending entries from the Offline Inbox, then fetches the message bodies by msg_id from the Message Store.
sonnet.q12: The event was not acked, so the bus redelivers it and another worker repeats the whole recipient list. Inbox puts are idempotent on (user_id, msg_id) and clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
